name: Mount Ishizuchi (石鎚山) from the ropeway
why: The highest peak in western Japan and a holy mountain of the yamabushi: through beech forest past mountain shrines, a choice of hanging iron chains, and a rock blade of a summit at 1,982 m.
book: Free. Ishizuchi Tozan Ropeway from Shimotani (bus from Iyo-Saijo station, about 1 hour), 7.5 minutes up, then 20 minutes to Jojusha. Huts and Ishizuchi Shrine's summit lodge (0897-55-4168) if you stay.
water: Food and drinks at Jojusha and at the summit lodge; rest huts on the way are not always open. Carry 1.5-2 litres.
dangers: The chains (33-74 m, near-vertical) are optional: bypass paths go round each one. Skip them in rain.
The ridge from the summit shrine to Tengudake is a narrow rock edge with drops on the north side: only in dry, calm weather.
Fog, wind and cold at the top; snow and ice from December to April.
turnaround: Not at Yoakashi pass by 12:00: turn back; the descent to the last ropeway car takes 2-2.5 hours.

points.name: Jojusha, above the ropeway
points.note: 1,450 m, 20 minutes' walk from the top station of the ropeway: the shrine, its inns and a window framing the summit's north face. The trail starts behind it, 3.6 km to the top.

points.name: Ishizuchi chains
points.note: Past the Yoakashi pass the first of three iron chains hangs down the rock, about 2 hours from Jojusha; a bypass path climbs beside it.

points.name: Misen summit shrine
points.note: 1,972 m: Ishizuchi Shrine's Chojosha and the summit lodge, with food and drinks. Many stop here.

points.name: Tengudake
points.note: 1,982 m, ten minutes along the rock edge from the shrine: the top of Shikoku, with cliffs falling north. Back the same way.
